_what: How a Trillion page in a browser hands what it shows to the Trillion Mac app on this computer (computer/open-from-web.mjs, started by the Mac helper). The helper listens on `host`:`port` (this computer only) and answers a page only when its Origin is exactly one of `allowed_origins` and its Host is this listener: GET /hello says the Mac app is here; POST /open { path } opens `path` inside the Mac app's menu bar panel (the trillion://panel address, macos/App/MenuBarPanel.swift). A path must start with `/`, name only the first folders in `open_folders`, hold only characters in `path_characters`, and be at most `most_path_characters` long; anything else is refused with the words in `words`. Each address carries a one-time `acknowledged.id_parameter` the app strips before it opens the screen; once the page inside the panel has taken the screen the app calls back GET `acknowledged.taken_path`?id= on this listener with the header `acknowledged.app_header` set to the app's bundle id (a web page cannot send that header: the browser's preflight is refused). The helper hands the address over again `every_ms` apart up to `most_attempts` times until that callback arrives (computer/deliver-until-acknowledged.mjs). The app's own address for the callback is in App/menu-bar-panel.json `acknowledge`, which must agree with `host`, `port` and these names (test/open-from-web.test.mjs). Origin is advisory against other programs on this computer: it keeps other web pages out, and what a program here could ask is only to open a Trillion screen the person can open anyway. `enabled` false closes the listener; `bundle_id` and `url_template` name the app and the address it takes.

words.not_allowed: That page is not allowed to ask this computer to open Trillion.
words.bad_path: That is not a Trillion screen this computer can open.
words.not_taken: The Trillion Mac app did not take it. Open Trillion and try again.
